info.title: Merchant API
info.description:
Generated from the proto contract (`merchant.*.v1`) by protoc-gen-fiber. Never edit it by hand.

- JSON is camelCase. Every documented key of a response is always present: an empty object or time is `null`, a list `[]`, a string `""`.
- Ids carry a prefix of their object kind (`pay_…`). Amounts are `Money` objects: a decimal string `value` and its `currency`.
- A field with a list of values may gain new values in v1: a client must accept a value it does not know.
- A request field the route does not declare is refused (`400 unknown_field`); a body that breaks a declared rule is refused with one `details` item per broken rule.
- Every error has one shape (`Error`), with a `type` per HTTP status and a stable `code`.

tags.name: TestFundsService
tags.description:
Sandbox test funds: money credited straight to your project's available
balance so you can try payouts without a pay-in first. The route exists
only in Sandbox, never Production: anywhere else it answers
`404 route_not_found`.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer sk_test_…`.

tags.name: DisputeService
tags.description:
Disputes are a payer's challenges of your payments, and reversals a
payment provider made without one. Providers report them and their
outcomes: you read them here, or learn of them from the
`dispute.opened` and `dispute.closed` webhooks. An open dispute holds
the disputed money from your balance until it is decided.

Authenticate with the secret API key of one project
(`Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` or `sk_test_…`). The key's project is
the only one you read: no request field names a merchant or a project,
and another project's dispute answers `404 dispute_not_found`.

tags.name: PaymentService
tags.description:
Payments collect money from a payer. Create a payment for the amount you
want, then start an attempt with the instrument the payer chose (a bank's
virtual account, QRIS, an e-wallet): the attempt's `nextAction` tells the
payer how to pay. A payment can take several attempts until one succeeds
or the payment expires. Learn the outcome from the `payment.paid` and
`payment.expired` webhooks, or read the payment again.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` (or `sk_test_…`).
Every create takes an `Idempotency-Key`: send the same key again after a
timeout or a 5xx and you get the first answer, with `Idempotent-Replayed:
true`, and nothing is created twice.

tags.name: PaymentLinkService
tags.description:
Payment links are shareable checkout pages that collect payments: create
one, share its `url`, and the payer picks how to pay on Zeny's page. Each
payment made through a link carries the link's id in `paymentLink`, so
the `payment.paid` webhook tells you which link was paid. The links live
in your API key's project; they behave as the dashboard's payment links
do.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` (or `sk_test_…`).
Create takes an `Idempotency-Key`: send the same key again after a
timeout or a 5xx and you get the first link, with `Idempotent-Replayed:
true`, and nothing is created twice.

tags.name: PayoutService
tags.description:
Payouts send money from your project's available balance to a saved
beneficiary's bank account or e-wallet. A payout you request reserves its
money at once and waits in `pending_approval` until the platform's team
approves it; it is then `processing` until the
provider reports it `paid` or `failed`. Learn the outcome from the
`payout.paid`, `payout.failed`, `payout.rejected` and `payout.canceled`
webhooks, or read the payout again.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` (or `sk_test_…`).
Every POST takes an `Idempotency-Key`: send the same key again after a
timeout or a 5xx and you get the first answer's status with the payout as
it is now, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and nothing happens twice.

get.description:
Lists your project's disputes, newest opened first, a page at a time.
A cursor is valid only with the status that issued it. A list never
counts.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only disputes in this status: open, won or lost. Omit it for every
status.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, at most 100; 0 or omitted means 20.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page; omit it for the first page.

get.description:
Retrieves one dispute of your project. An id your project does not
hold answers `404 dispute_not_found`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dispute's id (`dsp_…`).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only links in this status: active, closed or expired (an active or
closed link past its expiry). Omit it for every listed link.

parameters.name: createdFrom
parameters.description: Only links created at or after this RFC 3339 time.

parameters.name: createdTo
parameters.description: Only links created before this RFC 3339 time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, at most 100; 0 or omitted means 20.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page; omit it for the first page.

post.description:
Creates an active payment link. A business that is not live answers
`403 merchant_not_live`, and an archived project `403 project_archived`.
A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and
body answers the first link with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the key
with another body answers `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

get.description:
Retrieves one payment link of your project, a canceled one included.
A link of another project answers `404 payment_link_not_found`, as an
unknown id does.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link's id (`pl_…`).

post.description:
Cancels a link that took no payment: it is no longer listed and its
checkout page says it was canceled. A link that took any payment,
pending or paid, answers `409 payment_link_has_payments`: close it
instead. A canceled link is answered as it is. No `Idempotency-Key`,
as for close.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link's id (`pl_…`).

post.description:
Stops an active link taking payments. A link already closed, or past
its expiry, is answered as it is; a canceled one answers
`409 invalid_state_transition`. It moves no money and is idempotent by
state, so it takes no `Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link's id (`pl_…`).

post.description:
Lets a closed link take payments again. An active link is answered as
it is; one past its expiry, or canceled, answers
`409 invalid_state_transition`. A business that is not live answers
`403 merchant_not_live`, and an archived project `403 project_archived`.
No `Idempotency-Key`, as for close.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link's id (`pl_…`).

post.description:
Creates a payment the payer can then pay. Nothing is charged yet: start
an attempt next. The `reference` is your own order id and is unique in
the project; reusing it answers `409 duplicate_reference`, with the
existing payment's id in `error.details[0].id`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

get.description: Retrieves a payment of your project, with its latest attempt.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The payment's id (`pay_…`).

post.description:
Starts paying a pending payment with an instrument and returns the new
attempt. Show the payer its `nextAction`. When the payment provider
refuses the attempt, the answer is still `201`, with `status: "failed"`
and a `failure`: it is not an error, so do not retry the same request;
start a new attempt (with a new key), perhaps with another instrument.
An attempt whose outcome is not known yet is `processing`. A payment
with an attempt still open answers `409 attempt_in_progress`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The payment's id (`pay_…`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

schema.description: CreatePaymentAttemptRequest is how the payer chose to pay.

instrument.description:
The instrument's code: a bank for a virtual account ("BCA"), "QRIS",
or an e-wallet ("GOPAY"). Upper case letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

returnUrl.description:
Where a redirect sends the payer back to when they finish: an absolute
`https://` URL, at most 2048 characters. Omit it to let the provider
decide.

post.description:
Requests a payout and reserves its money (`debit`) from the project's
available balance. The `reference` is your own id and is unique in the
project; reusing it answers `409 duplicate_reference`, with the existing
payout's id in `error.details[0].id`. The beneficiary must exist
(`404 beneficiary_not_found`), not be deleted (`409
beneficiary_deleted`) and have a passing name check
(`409 name_check_required`, `409 name_check_failed`; `409
name_check_pending` while staff verify the account by hand). The balance must
cover the debit (`409 insufficient_balance`), and the amount the fee
when the beneficiary bears it (`400 amount_below_fee`). A merchant that
cannot send money now is `403 merchant_not_live`, an archived project
`403 project_archived`, and a merchant that owes the platform
`409 outstanding_debt`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

get.description: Retrieves a payout of your project.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The payout's id (`po_…`).

post.description:
Cancels a payout still waiting for approval and returns it, `canceled`:
its debit goes back to the available balance. A payout that left
`pending_approval` cannot be canceled (`409 invalid_state_transition`),
and neither can one canceled already under another key; a retry with
the same key answers the canceled payout.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The payout's id (`po_…`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

schema.description: CancelPayoutRequest names the payout to cancel.

post.description:
Credits test funds to the project's available balance and answers
them. The amount is whole rupiah in IDR, at least Rp 1.000 and at most
Rp 100.000.000 per request, and at most Rp 1.000.000.000 per project a
day (Asia/Jakarta). Above either limit it is
`409 test_funds_limit_exceeded` on `amount.value`; when Sandbox has no
payout account to hold the money it is `409 test_funds_unavailable`.
The balance and the statement (a "Test funds" line) show the money at
once. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and body
answers the same test funds with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and
nothing is credited twice.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose, unique per request you mean (FIN-001): 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, kept at least 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body answers with the first status and the object as it stands now, and nothing is done twice; the same key with another body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

post.description:
DisputeEvent is the body of a webhook about a dispute.
It arrives as a signed POST to your endpoint.

The body's `type` and the `Webhook-Event` header are `dispute.closed`. Verify `Webhook-Signature` over the raw body before you trust it, store the event under its `id`, then answer any `2xx`.

parameters.name: Webhook-Signature
parameters.description: `sha256=` and the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `Webhook-Timestamp`, a period and the raw body, keyed with the whole endpoint secret (`whsec_…` included).

parameters.name: Webhook-Timestamp
parameters.description: When this try was signed, in Unix seconds: reject one more than five minutes old.

parameters.name: Webhook-Event
parameters.description: The event type, the body's `type`.

parameters.name: Webhook-Id
parameters.description: The event's id, the body's `id` (`evt_…`): the same on every try.

parameters.name: Webhook-Delivery
parameters.description: This delivery's id: one per endpoint the event goes to. Never deduplicate on it; use `Webhook-Id`.

2XX.description: Received. Answer once the event is stored; without a `2xx` it is tried again, up to 12 times over 10 to 20 hours.

Error.description: The error of every non-2xx answer, under the key `error`.

type.description: The class of the error, one per HTTP status.

code.description: A stable snake_case code to branch on (`unknown_field`, `too_long`, `payment_not_found`). New codes may be added in v1.

message.description: English, safe to show; never branch on it.

param.description: The request field the error is about, as a JSON path (`amount.value`, `items[1].name`, `metadata.*`).

details.description: One item per broken rule of a refused request; `[]` otherwise.

param.description: The field the item is about.

code.description: The rule's family: `field_required`, `too_short`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`, `value_not_allowed`, `out_of_range`, `too_few_items`, `too_many_items`, `duplicate_items` or `invalid_value`; or a domain code (`duplicate_reference`).

id.description: The public id of an existing object the item points at (`duplicate_reference`).

merchant.balance.v1.CreateTestFundsReque.description: CreateTestFundsRequest is the amount to credit.

amount.description: The amount to credit, whole rupiah in IDR.

merchant.balance.v1.TestFunds.description: TestFunds is one Sandbox test funds credit.

merchant.payment.v1.CardMethod.description:
CardMethod is a card paid on the provider's page. It has no detail yet;
fields arrive by addition.

merchant.payment.v1.CreatePaymentLinkReq.description: CreatePaymentLinkRequest is the payment link to create.

name.description:
What the payer sees the link is for: 1 to 120 characters once the
spaces around it are trimmed, no control characters.

amount.description:
What every payer pays: a positive IDR amount with at most 2 decimals.
Omit it, or send `null`, to let the payer enter the amount.

instruments.description:
The instruments the payer may choose from ("BCA", "QRIS", "GOPAY"),
at most 30, each once: virtual accounts, QRIS and e-wallets. Omit it,
or send `[]`, to offer every instrument the payer can use.

successRedirectUrl.description:
Your page for a payer who paid: an absolute `https` URL, at most 2048
characters. Omit it for none.

expiresAt.description:
When the link stops taking payments, in the future. Omit it, or send
`null`, for a link that never expires.

merchant.payment.v1.CreatePaymentRequest.description: CreatePaymentRequest is the payment you ask the payer for.

reference.description:
Your own id for the order, unique in the project: printable text, at
most 100 characters.

amount.description:
What the payer pays: a positive amount with at most the currency's
decimals (IDR: 2).

description.description:
Shown to the payer on the hosted page and passed to the payment
provider; at most 500 characters.

payer.description:
Who pays, when you know it. Some instruments need the payer's name or
contact; it is passed to the payment provider and never shown to others.

metadata.description:
Your own key-value labels, returned as sent: at most 20 keys, a key of
1 to 40 characters and a value of at most 500. Never put personal data
here.

expiresAt.description:
When the payment stops taking attempts: between 5 minutes and 30 days
from now. Omit it for 24 hours.

merchant.payment.v1.Dispute.description:
Dispute is a payer's dispute of one of your payments, or a reversal the
payment provider made without one. Each field a payment's
`disputes[]` summary carries has the same name and value here. Every
amount is in the payment's currency.

type.description:
dispute: the payer disputed the payment. reversal: the provider took
the money back without a dispute. Accept a value you do not know yet.

status.description:
open: under review, the disputed money is held (`frozenAmount`). won:
decided for you, the hold is released. lost: decided for the payer,
the amount was taken from your balance. Accept a value you do not know
yet.

amount.description:
What is disputed, in the payment's currency: the same figure as the
payment's `disputes[].amount`.

frozenAmount.description:
What the dispute holds from your balance now; `0.00` once decided, or
while the payment has not settled (the dispute then postpones its
settlement instead).

shortfallAmount.description:
What your balance could not cover yet when the dispute opened, less
what later settlements covered; `0.00` when covered or decided.

resolvedAt.description: When it was decided; `null` while open.

merchant.payment.v1.DisputeEvent.description:
DisputeEvent is the body of a webhook about a dispute.
It arrives as a signed POST to your endpoint.

id.description:
The event's id (`evt_…`), also sent as `Webhook-Id`: the same on every
try. Store events under it, once: one can arrive twice.

apiVersion.description: The API version `data.object` is written in ("v1").

mode.description:
live from the production API (`sk_live_` keys), test from the sandbox
(`sk_test_` keys). Accept a value you do not know yet.

resourceVersion.description:
Orders the events of one object: drop an event whose resourceVersion is
older than the one you hold. A JSON number, not a string.

merchant.payment.v1.DisputeEvent.Data.description: Data holds the object the event is about.

object.description: The dispute as `GET /disputes/{id}` answered when the event was written.

merchant.payment.v1.DisputeSummary.description: DisputeSummary is a dispute of the payment, in short.

type.description:
dispute: the payer disputed the payment. reversal: the provider took
the money back without a dispute.

status.description:
open: under review, the disputed money is held. won: decided for you,
the hold is released. lost: decided for the payer, the amount was
taken from your balance.

amount.description: What is disputed, in the payment's currency.

resolvedAt.description: When it was decided; `null` while open.

merchant.payment.v1.Fee.description: Fee is one line the capture took from the payment's amount.

type.description:
fee: the platform's fee. tax: the tax on that fee. conversion: the estimated cost
of converting a payment charged in another currency. cost: a provider
cost passed on to you.

amount.description: The line's amount, in the payment's currency.

merchant.payment.v1.ListDisputesResponse.description: ListDisputesResponse is a page of disputes.

nextCursor.description: The cursor of the next page; "" on the last page.

merchant.payment.v1.ListPaymentLinksResp.description: ListPaymentLinksResponse is a page of payment links (API-001 §4.4).

nextCursor.description: The cursor of the next page; "" on the last page.

merchant.payment.v1.Payer.description: Payer is who pays a payment. Every field is optional.

name.description: The payer's name, at most 255 characters.

phone.description: The payer's phone number: 6 to 20 digits with an optional leading `+`.

merchant.payment.v1.PayerInput.description: Payer is who pays a payment. Every field is optional.

name.description: The payer's name, at most 255 characters.

phone.description: The payer's phone number: 6 to 20 digits with an optional leading `+`.

merchant.payment.v1.Payment.description:
Payment is money you asked a payer for. Its `status` is `pending` until an
attempt captures it (`paid`) or it expires unpaid (`expired`). A payment
that expired can still become `paid` when the provider reports a capture
late: money that arrived is never ignored.

reference.description: Your own id for the order, as you sent it.

amount.description: What you asked the payer to pay.

amountReceived.description:
What the payment actually collected: `0.00` until it is paid, then the
amount.

status.description: pending, paid or expired. Accept a value you do not know yet.

captureMethod.description: automatic: the payment is captured as soon as the payer pays.

description.description: As you sent it; "" when none.

payer.description:
Who pays, as you sent it (or as the payer typed it on a hosted page);
`null` when nothing is known.

latestAttempt.description: The newest attempt at paying; `null` before the first.

fees.description:
What the capture charged you, one line per kind; `[]` until the
payment is paid. A fee the payer bears is not a line.

net.description:
What you receive: the amount less every fee line; `null` until the
payment is paid.

settlement.description:
When the money becomes your available balance; `null` until the payment
is paid.

disputes.description: The payment's disputes and reversals, oldest first; `[]` when none.

paymentLink.description:
The payment link (`pl_…`) the payer paid through; "" for a payment you
created with this API.

paidAt.description: When it was paid; `null` until then.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentAttempt.description:
PaymentAttempt is one try at paying a payment with one instrument.
requires_action: the payer must act (see `nextAction`). processing: the
outcome is not known yet; wait for the webhook or read it again, never
start another attempt meanwhile. succeeded: the payer paid. failed: it
did not go through (see `failure`); the payment can take a new attempt.
expired: the payer did not pay in time.

status.description:
requires_action, processing, succeeded, failed or expired. Accept a
value you do not know yet.

charge.description:
What the payer is charged: the payment's amount, plus the fee when the
payer bears it, in the currency the provider charges.

nextAction.description: What the payer does next; `null` unless the status is requires_action.

failure.description: Why the attempt failed; `null` unless the status is failed.

expiresAt.description:
When the payer's instructions stop working; `null` until the provider
gave them.

uniqueCode.description:
The unique code added to `charge` so the payment can be told apart by
its amount, on a payment method whose provider reports no reference;
`null` on every other attempt. It is already in `charge`, is paid by
the payer and kept by the platform, and is never taken from the payment's
amount: it is not a fee and does not change `net`.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentAttemptEvent.description:
PaymentAttemptEvent is the body of a webhook about one attempt at paying a payment:
`payment_attempt.failed` means the payment can still be paid by another
attempt.
It arrives as a signed POST to your endpoint.

id.description:
The event's id (`evt_…`), also sent as `Webhook-Id`: the same on every
try. Store events under it, once: one can arrive twice.

apiVersion.description: The API version `data.object` is written in ("v1").

mode.description:
live from the production API (`sk_live_` keys), test from the sandbox
(`sk_test_` keys). Accept a value you do not know yet.

resourceVersion.description:
Orders the events of one object: drop an event whose resourceVersion is
older than the one you hold. A JSON number, not a string.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentAttemptEvent..description: Data holds the object the event is about.

object.description:
The attempt as `POST /payments/{id}/attempts` answers it, when the
event was written.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentEvent.description:
PaymentEvent is the body of a webhook about a payment.
It arrives as a signed POST to your endpoint.

id.description:
The event's id (`evt_…`), also sent as `Webhook-Id`: the same on every
try. Store events under it, once: one can arrive twice.

apiVersion.description: The API version `data.object` is written in ("v1").

mode.description:
live from the production API (`sk_live_` keys), test from the sandbox
(`sk_test_` keys). Accept a value you do not know yet.

resourceVersion.description:
Orders the events of one object: drop an event whose resourceVersion is
older than the one you hold. A JSON number, not a string.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentEvent.Data.description: Data holds the object the event is about.

object.description: The payment as `GET /payments/{id}` answered when the event was written.

merchant.payment.v1.PaymentLink.description:
PaymentLink is a shareable checkout page that collects payments for your
project. Each payer who pays through it makes a payment whose
`paymentLink` is the link's id.

name.description: What the payer sees the link is for.

amount.description: What every payer pays; `null` when the payer enters the amount.

status.description:
active: takes payments. closed: takes none; reopen it to take them
again. expired: past `expiresAt`, takes none and cannot be reopened.
canceled: canceled before it took any payment; final. Accept a value
you do not know yet.

instruments.description:
The instruments the payer may choose from, in code order; `[]` offers
every instrument the payer can use.

successRedirectUrl.description: Your page for a payer who paid; "" when none.

url.description: The checkout page to share with payers.

paidCount.description: How many payments through the link were paid.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops taking payments; `null` when it never does.

type.description:
va, qris, ewallet, card, bank_transfer, crypto or paypal. Accept a value
you do not know yet.

instrument.description: The instrument's code, as you sent it ("BCA", "QRIS", "GOPAY").

merchant.payment.v1.QrisMethod.description:
QrisMethod is a QRIS code any Indonesian banking or e-wallet app pays.
It has no detail yet; fields arrive by addition.

merchant.payment.v1.Settlement.description: Settlement is when a paid payment's money becomes your available balance.

status.description:
pending: waiting for `dueAt`. settled: in your available balance. An
open dispute may hold the money past `dueAt`.

dueAt.description: When the money is due to settle.

merchant.payment.v1.VaMethod.description: VaMethod is a bank virtual account.

accountNumberLast4.description: The account number's last four digits.

merchant.payout.v1.CreatePayoutRequest.description: CreatePayoutRequest is the payout you ask for.

reference.description:
Your own id for the payout, unique in the project: 1 to 64 printable
ASCII characters once surrounding spaces are trimmed (banks and vendors
accept no more).

amount.description:
What to pay out: a positive amount with at most the currency's
decimals (IDR: 2). Only fiat currencies are paid out.

description.description: Your own note on the payout, at most 255 characters.

merchant.payout.v1.Destination.description:
Destination is the account a payout is sent to. `type` names it; exactly
the sub-object of that name is set, every other one is `null`. The full
account number is never answered.

type.description: bank_account or ewallet. Accept a value you do not know yet.

holderName.description: The account holder's name, as saved on the beneficiary.

accountNumberLast4.description: The account number's last four digits.

merchant.payout.v1.Fee.description: Fee is one line the platform charges for a payout.

type.description: fee: the platform's fee. tax: the tax on that fee.

amount.description: The line's amount, in the payout's currency.

merchant.payout.v1.Payout.description:
Payout is money sent from your balance to a beneficiary. Its money always
adds up: `debit` = `net` + the sum of `fees`. A fee you bear is debited on
top of the amount (`net` = `amount`); one the beneficiary bears comes off
what is sent (`debit` = `amount`).

pending_approval: waiting for a second person on your team. processing:
approved, being sent. paid: the provider reported the money sent.
failed: it was not sent (see `failure`); the debit is back in your
balance. rejected: your approver refused it, or the platform's risk review did.
canceled: you withdrew it before approval. returned: the bank sent the
money back after it was paid (not sent yet; handle it from the start).

reference.description:
Your own id for the payout, as you sent it with surrounding spaces
trimmed.

amount.description: What you asked to pay out.

fees.description:
The platform's fee and its tax for the payout, whoever bears them: both lines
are always listed, `0.00` when the payout is free.

debit.description:
What leaves your available balance: reserved when you request the
payout, returned in full when it ends unpaid.

destination.description:
Where the money goes, as it was paid: a beneficiary never changes, and
a deleted one keeps its payouts' destination.

status.description:
pending_approval, processing, paid, failed, rejected, canceled or
returned. Accept a value you do not know yet.

failure.description:
Why the payout failed; `null` unless the status is failed. declined:
every provider it was sent to refused it, so check the beneficiary's
account. processing_error: it failed after a provider took it.

description.description: As you sent it; "" when none.

paidAt.description: When the provider reported the money sent; `null` until then.

type.description:
withdrawal: your own balance to your own withdraw account, requested on the dashboard.
disbursement: money sent to someone else, as every payout this API creates is. Each has its own fee. Accept
a value you do not know yet.

merchant.payout.v1.PayoutEvent.description:
PayoutEvent is the body of a webhook about a payout.
It arrives as a signed POST to your endpoint.

id.description:
The event's id (`evt_…`), also sent as `Webhook-Id`: the same on every
try. Store events under it, once: one can arrive twice.

apiVersion.description: The API version `data.object` is written in ("v1").

mode.description:
live from the production API (`sk_live_` keys), test from the sandbox
(`sk_test_` keys). Accept a value you do not know yet.

resourceVersion.description:
Orders the events of one object: drop an event whose resourceVersion is
older than the one you hold. A JSON number, not a string.

merchant.payout.v1.PayoutEvent.Data.description: Data holds the object the event is about.

object.description: The payout as `GET /payouts/{id}` answered when the event was written.

type.v1.DisplayQr.description: DisplayQr is a QR code the payer scans with a banking or e-wallet app.

data.description:
The QR payload (EMVCo QRIS string). Render it as a QR code; never
change it.

type.v1.DisplayVa.description: DisplayVa is a virtual account the payer transfers the exact charge to.

number.description: The virtual account number to transfer to.

billerCode.description:
The company code some banks ask for before the number (a Mandiri bill
payment); "" when the bank asks for none.

type.v1.Failure.description:
Failure is why something a provider was asked to do did not happen: a
refused payment attempt, a business verification the identity checks
turned down, later a failed payout or refund (API-001 §4.3 rule 2). It
is not an HTTP error: the request that started it succeeded, and the
object's status says it failed. `code` is the platform's normalized code,
never a provider's, and the list grows by addition: handle a code you do
not know as `processing_error`.

code.description:
declined: the provider refused it (a payment: the payer may try
another instrument; a verification: a check refused the evidence).
processing_error: it failed for another reason after it was sent.

message.description:
A short English explanation, safe to show to the person who sent it
(the payer, the merchant). Branch on `code`, never on this text.

type.v1.Money.description:
Money is an amount with its currency (API-001 §4.1, FIN-002). Every amount
on the wire is a Money, even next to another one in the same currency, so
a client never pairs a bare number with a currency it guessed.

value.description:
A decimal string at the asset's fixed scale ("150000.00" for IDR), with
no thousands separator: never a float or integer minor units, because
crypto assets need up to 18 decimals. Input with more decimals than the
scale is refused (400 invalid_amount), never rounded.

currency.description:
The public asset code ("IDR"). A code that has appeared in the API never
changes; renaming an asset adds an alias.

type.v1.MoneyInput.description:
Money is an amount with its currency (API-001 §4.1, FIN-002). Every amount
on the wire is a Money, even next to another one in the same currency, so
a client never pairs a bare number with a currency it guessed.

value.description:
A decimal string at the asset's fixed scale ("150000.00" for IDR), with
no thousands separator: never a float or integer minor units, because
crypto assets need up to 18 decimals. Input with more decimals than the
scale is refused (400 invalid_amount), never rounded.

currency.description:
The public asset code ("IDR"). A code that has appeared in the API never
changes; renaming an asset adds an alias.

type.v1.NextAction.description:
NextAction is what the payer does next to pay an attempt (API-001 §4.3
rule 4). `type` says which one; exactly the sub-object of that name is
set, every other one is `null`. New types arrive by addition: a client
shows what it knows and treats an unknown type as "send the payer to the
hosted page".

type.description:
display_va: show a virtual account number the payer transfers to.
display_qr: render a QR code (QRIS) the payer scans.
redirect: send the payer to a URL (an e-wallet or a bank's page).
open_app: open the payer's app with a deep link (reserved, not sent in
v1).

type.v1.Redirect.description: Redirect sends the payer to a page that takes the payment.

ServerError.description: `api_error` (500): our failure, safe to retry with the same Idempotency-Key; `provider_unavailable` (503): a payment provider is down, retry later with the same key; `overloaded` (503): the API is busy and ran nothing, retry after `Retry-After` with the same key.

X-Request-ID.description: The request's id: quote it to support. Sent on every response.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per window, on every answer of a route with a declared rate limit.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this answer replays an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key: nothing was created or sent again. Absent on a first answer.

bearerAuth.description: A merchant API key on the merchant API; a session token on the dashboard and console APIs; a service key of the platform's own (`zsk_…`) on the service and agent APIs.
